title: Zigzag Conversion
interviewTips: Ask if numRows == 1 or numRows >= len(s) should return s directly without simulation
Trade-off: 2D grid is intuitive but wastes space scanning empty cells, row-buckets achieve O(n) time with O(n) space and no empty scan
Edge-case tip: direction must flip at row 0 and row numRows-1, and test with numRows=1, numRows=2, and single character

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force with 2D Grid Simulation
approaches.intuition: Literally draw the zigzag on paper with rows and columns, place each character by moving down vertically then up diagonally, then read row by row.
approaches.theory: Maintain row,col pointer and going_down flag. Place s[i] at grid[row][col]. If row==0 go down, if row==numRows-1 go up. Going down means row+1 same col, going up means row-1 col+1. After all placed, iterate rows 0..numRows-1 and columns 0..n-1 collecting non-empty cells to form answer.

timeComplexity.explanation: O(n) to place characters plus O(numRows * n) to scan entire grid row by row for non-empty cells.

spaceComplexity.explanation: 2D grid of numRows rows by n columns to hold sparse zigzag layout plus output string.

steps: grid 3 x 14 empty, row=0 col=0 going_down=True
place P(0,0) A(1,0) Y(2,0) then flip to up, place P(1,1)
place A(0,2) L(1,2) I(2,2) then flip to up, place S(1,3)
place H(0,4) I(1,4) R(2,4) then flip to up, place I(1,5)
place N(0,6) G(1,6), read row0=PAHN row1=APLSIIG row2=YIR

edgeCases: numRows == 1 returns original string, avoids infinite direction flip
numRows >= len(s) returns original string, each char in own row
single character string with any numRows

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Row Buckets with Direction Flag
approaches.intuition: We only care about which row each character belongs to, not its column, so append characters directly to per-row buffers while bouncing between top and bottom.
approaches.theory: Zigzag row index follows periodic bounce: 0,1,...,numRows-1,numRows-2,...,1,0,... Maintain cur row and going_down flag. For each ch append to rows[cur], then update flag at boundaries and do cur+=1 or cur-=1. Finally join rows in order. This is exact row projection of grid simulation without storing columns.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single pass over n characters, each append is O(1) amortized, final join is O(n).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Row buffers together store all n characters plus output string, no empty grid cells.

steps: P->row0 A->row1 Y->row2 P->row1 A->row0 L->row1 I->row2
S->row1 H->row0 I->row1 R->row2 I->row1 N->row0 G->row1

edgeCases: numRows == 1 must early return else cur would go out of bounds
numRows == 2 alternates 0,1,0,1 with no diagonal middle row
len(s) <= numRows means cur never hits bottom, just fills top rows
